name: Scandinavian Defense
summary: The Scandinavian (1...d5) challenges e4 at once; after 2.exd5 Qxd5 the queen recaptures and sidesteps to a5.
intro: The Scandinavian Defense, 1.e4 d5, is the most direct way to challenge White’s king-pawn. After 2.exd5 Qxd5 3.Nc3 Qa5 Black obtains a solid, if slightly passive, structure and an easy-to-learn set-up that avoids reams of theory.
line: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5

sections.heading: Strategic ideas
paragraphs: The Scandinavian Defense, also called the Center Counter, meets 1.e4 with the immediate 1...d5, directly challenging White's centre on the first move. After 2.exd5 Black usually recaptures at once with 2...Qxd5, bringing the queen into play early. White gains a tempo by attacking the queen with 3.Nc3, and Black retreats to a safe square, most commonly 3...Qa5.

The appeal of the Scandinavian is its directness and clarity: Black removes White's e-pawn and reaches a sound, if slightly passive, structure with little of the memorization demanded by many 1.e4 defenses. The recurring theme is that Black trades a small loss of time for a simple, principled position, then develops harmoniously and looks to complete a solid setup.

sections.heading: Early queen development
paragraphs: Bringing the queen out on move two runs counter to the usual advice against early queen sorties, but here it is justified because the queen has good retreat squares and is not easily harassed with further tempo gains. From a5 the queen eyes the e1-a5 diagonal and supports queenside development, while the alternative retreat to d6 keeps the queen more centralized and flexible. White's extra tempo is real but modest, and Black's structure remains healthy.

After 3...Qa5 Black typically continues with ...Nf6, ...c6 to give the queen a retreat and bolster d5, ...Bf5 or ...Bg4 to develop the light-squared bishop actively, and then ...e6, ...Be7 and castling. The setup is compact and easy to remember, which is a major reason the Scandinavian is popular among club players and as a practical surprise weapon.

keyIdeas: 1...d5 challenges White's centre immediately and eliminates the e-pawn
Recapturing 2...Qxd5 develops the queen but invites 3.Nc3 with tempo
The ...Qa5 retreat keeps the queen safe and active on the queenside
Black trades a little time for a clear, solid structure
The ...c6 move gives the queen a retreat and supports the d5 square
Active development of the light-squared bishop to f5 or g4 is a core plan

white: Develop with tempo by hitting Black's queen, starting with 3.Nc3
Build a central pawn and piece presence with d4 and natural development
Aim to exploit the small lead in development and space
Consider harassing the black queen or the bishop to gain further time
Castle and prepare central or kingside expansion
black: Recapture with 2...Qxd5 and retreat the queen to a safe square like a5
Play ...c6 to give the queen a retreat and support the d5 square
Develop the light-squared bishop actively to f5 or g4 before ...e6
Seek a solid, balanced middlegame and gradual queenside counterplay
